title: Mount Sinai
lead: The mountain where God met Moses in the burning bush and gave Israel the covenant and the Ten Words (Exodus 3; 19–24). Also called Horeb, it was revisited by Elijah (1 Kings 19), and its site is still debated.

sections.h: Sinai and Horeb across the Bible
sections.b: The mountain has two names. Exodus mostly says Sinai, while Deuteronomy calls it Horeb, and the burning bush stands at "God's mountain, toward Horeb" (Exodus 3:1). Israel camps there from Exodus 19 to Numbers 10, almost a year. Old poems picture the LORD marching from Sinai, Seir or Teman (Deuteronomy 33:2; Judges 5:4–5; Psalm 68:8; Habakkuk 3:3). Elijah flees to Horeb, where God speaks not in wind, quake or fire but in "a sound of thin silence" (1 Kings 19:8–12). In the New Testament Stephen recalls Moses at Sinai (Acts 7:30–38), Paul makes Sinai a figure of the old covenant (Galatians 4:24–25), and Hebrews sets it against Mount Zion (Hebrews 12:18–24).
